markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Normal (75%)** · Unreliable input · Careful review
Reliability flag, a two-class set and second-model disagreement undercut this call.

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Normal 75%, Benign 25%, others <1% | Normal leads; Benign plausible |
| Conformal set | Normal, Benign (90% level) | Cannot separate the two |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.15 / 8th percentile | Input flagged as suspect |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | No | Top classes differ |
| Similar cases | 4 of 5 Normal [F5] | Mostly supports Normal |

## Tissue evidence
- **Normal lobules, two-layered epithelium** (regions 9, 10, 11) · ↓ invasive · Strongest benign association, but failed spot check (0/20) [F2] · Unreliable
- **Gland / tubule formation** (regions 2, 5, 6) · ↓ invasive · Above-typical score; associated with lower invasive likelihood [F4] · Weak
- **Tumor-infiltrating stroma** (region 3) · ↑ invasive · Small positive term; no strong invasive signal · Validated
- **Lymphocytic infiltrate** (region 6) · context · Below-typical score; descriptive only [F3] · Weak

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion effect 0.002 (CI −0.005 to 0.007) includes 0: not shown to reflect the classifier. Normal lobules (0/20) is Unreliable.

## Could be wrong if
- Stain degradation (severity 3) distorts embeddings; reliability is only 15%.
- Benign is the true class: it holds 25% and the second model disagrees.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 9, 10, 11** — Confirm two-layered lobular epithelium; this concept failed its spot check.
2. **Regions 2, 5, 6** — Look for glandular atypia that separates Normal from Benign.
3. **Region 3** — Rule out stromal infiltration; strongest tumor-infiltrating stroma score here.
